an3.73:1.6: Here, “immersion” means “serenity” (_samatha_), and “knowledge” is “discernment” (_ñāṇa_), two complementary dimensions of Buddhist meditation. See [an2.31:1.1]() and notes.
an3.73:1.7: In most presentations, immersion or serenity appears first—the three trainings, the five faculties, the four bases of psychic power, the gradual training, and so on. However, in some cases, the wisdom factor is presented first—right view as the start of the eightfold path, or investigation of principles as the first of the seven awakening factors. Ānanda discusses this issue also in [an4.170]().
